meta.title: The 50-Mile Strip Where You Can Legally Get Away With Murder #shorts
meta.description:
Imagine standing in a beautiful, fifty-square-mile section of Yellowstone National Park where the law literally does not apply. It sounds like a movie, but it is a real constitutional loophole. This area lies in Idaho, but the federal court district covers all of Yellowstone, which is in Wyoming. Under the Sixth Amendment, if you commit a major crime here, you have the right to a jury from both the state and district where the crime occurred. But here is the catch: absolutely nobody lives in this specific strip of Idaho forest. No population means no jury can ever be formed. Since a trial is impossible, prosecutors might have to let you go entirely free. Would you ever dare to camp in this lawless zone? Comment below and follow for more bizarre secrets!
